entries.title: System Shock
entries.definitive_edition: System Shock: Enhanced Edition on Windows PC

emulation.notes: Use Enhanced Edition rather than manually emulating the DOS release.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Faithful classic presentation with modern controls and resolution support.

primary.why: The Windows PC Enhanced Edition is the best route for the original 1994 game because Nightdive's source-port release preserves the classic game while adding modern-system support, higher-resolution display options, widescreen support, mouselook, remappable controls, and the original Classic version.
primary.how_to_play: Buy System Shock: Enhanced Edition on Steam or GOG and play the Enhanced Edition for the classic game; keep the included Classic version only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate this original-game route with the 2023 remake; treat the remake as its own entry.

entries.title: System Shock
entries.definitive_edition: System Shock remake on Windows PC

emulation.notes: Use the native PC remake; no console emulation route is needed.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native Unreal Engine 4 PC remake presentation.

primary.why: The Windows PC release is the best route for the 2023 remake because it launched first, has PC capture/settings flexibility, and remains the highest-fidelity route compared with the later console and Switch ports. This is a remake entry, not a replacement listing for the 1994 original.
primary.how_to_play: Buy the 2023 System Shock remake on Steam or GOG and play the Windows PC build. Keep it separate from the original Enhanced Edition entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is the 2023 remake, distinct from System Shock: Enhanced Edition. Planned macOS and Linux ports were cancelled.

entries.title: System Shock 2
entries.definitive_edition: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster on Windows PC

emulation.notes: Use the remaster rather than manually configuring the 1999 release unless you specifically want historical comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Nightdive remaster with mod support and modernized multiplayer.

primary.why: The Windows PC 25th Anniversary Remaster is the best route because it modernizes the classic with Nightdive's KEX tech, improved compatibility, mod support, and restored/modernized cooperative multiplayer while preserving the original game structure.
primary.how_to_play: Buy System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster on Steam or GOG and play the Windows PC build. Play solo first for the intended horror pacing; use co-op later if desired.

entries.remaster_caveats: Dreamcast and VR versions were not released; use the 25th Anniversary Remaster for the current complete route.
